chapter: Cotton Club and radio fame with Cab
title: Harold Arlen, 'Stormy Weather', Ethel Waters and Lena Horne
summary: Thomas and Hinton recall Arlen writing Cotton Club shows, Ethel Waters introducing 'Stormy Weather', and Lena Horne copying her.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, this is where you and I come in together, is when we're coming downtown to 48th and Broadway.
Right. So we went downtown, and they got... Harold Arlen was the guy that wrote the shows uptown, because the first big show he...
No, he didn't write it for Lena.
Who did he write it for?
Ethel Waters. And Ethel Waters sang better than anybody ever sang it. And then Ethel Waters left to do that show, and Lena made the picture. And Lena didn't sing
too bad. Lena sang all right. Lena...

Yeah, she copied as much as she could. Because she was a little girl that was in the show at the Cotton Club. She copied as good as she could from Ethel Waters. And remember, she was a songstress with Noble Sissle's band. And bands had made more singers than anybody you could know.
